Title: Grab, govt join forces on RM160mil gig worker welfare package
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Grab Malaysia is working with the government to co-fund a RM160 million package aimed at boosting gig workers' earnings, reducing operating costs and strengthening social protection.
Under the initiative announced in the 2027 Budget, the median monthly net income of e-hailing drivers is expected to increase by up to RM227, while p-hailing delivery riders could earn up to RM100 more.
To boost earnings, the government and Grab have proposed minimum baseline rates for e-hailing and p-hailing workers, with adjustments expected to take effect in 2027.
Grab said the proposed rates would increase workers' take-home earnings while keeping passenger fares stable during the implementation of the framework.
The Gig Consultative Council will continue deliberations to determine the final rates.
The package also includes a government co-funded vehicle maintenance subsidy, starting with lubricants, which Grab said could reduce operating costs for drivers and delivery riders by up to 35 per cent.
Grab will introduce an interim safety incentive to reduce e-hailing insurance costs by up to 25 per cent for drivers with good safety scores.
The government and Grab will also support mandatory contributions to the Social Security Organisation.
Grab's most active drivers and delivery riders will receive full contribution subsidies, while other partners will receive subsidies of up to 50 per cent.
The initiative aims to strengthen social protection without reducing workers' take-home earnings.
Separately, Grab will partner with the government to introduce a dedicated first- and last-mile monthly transit pass, starting in the Klang Valley.
The pass will offer discounted e-hailing rides to and from train stations, improving access to public transport while generating additional demand for drivers.
"Improving the livelihoods of our driver- and delivery-partners has always been an important priority for Grab. We understand that every ringgit matters, whether it comes from additional earning opportunities or savings on the everyday costs of working.
"In collaboration with the government, we are taking the lead in the industry to advance measures that can make a meaningful difference to our partners, while building a stronger and more sustainable gig economy," said Grab Malaysia executive director Rashid Shukor.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in tabling the 2027 Budget, said the government was committed to safeguarding the welfare of 600,000 gig workers through more comprehensive protection.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Fomca welcomes education funding, flags rising school costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) has welcomed the substantial allocation for education under the 2027 Budget, but cautioned that parents continue to face rising school-related expenses.
Its chief executive officer Dr Saravanan Thambirajah said Fomca welcomed investments in school infrastructure, repairs to dilapidated schools, maintenance, early schooling assistance and supplementary food programmes.
"Education is a fundamental right, and access to quality education should not depend on a family's financial position.
"However, Fomca wishes to highlight that parents continue to face increasing school-related expenses, including uniforms, transportation, learning materials, extracurricular activities and other contributions," he said.
He said the government should ensure that school infrastructure was safe and properly maintained, particularly electrical wiring, toilets, water supply, classrooms and other essential facilities.
"Every allocation for school improvements must be closely monitored to ensure that projects are completed on time and meet the required standards," he said.
On higher education, technical and vocational education and training (TVET) and youth employment, he said Fomca supported initiatives to assist National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) borrowers, expand TVET and create more jobs for young Malaysians.
"The RM8 billion allocation for TVET and the target of creating 30,000 new employment opportunities are encouraging developments," he said.
However, he cautioned that training programmes had to be aligned with actual industry requirements.
"Young Malaysians should not be encouraged to enrol in training programmes that do not lead to meaningful employment or reasonable wages," he said.
He  called for stronger monitoring of training institutions, programme quality, fees and graduate employability.
"The objective must be to create a skilled workforce capable of securing sustainable employment and better incomes," he said.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of the 2027 Budget said the Education Ministry will receive the largest allocation of nearly RM69 billion.
He said the government had
agreed to double the allocation
for the repair and maintenance of all types of schools to RM2 billion, up from RM1 billion previously.
The Higher Education Ministry meanwhile will receive RM19.1 billion, including RM800 million to improve infrastructure such as lecture halls and student accommodation and to replace outdated equipment.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Mah Sing hails measures to boost housing affordability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mah Sing Group Bhd welcomed the 2027 Budget measures to ease living costs and improve housing affordability by boosting household disposable income, reducing upfront homebuying costs and widening access to housing financing.
"These initiatives are particularly timely in supporting first-time homebuyers and middle-income households, while providing positive momentum for Malaysia's residential property market," said Mah Sing founder and group managing director Tan Sri Leong Hoy Kum.
Leong said the group was also encouraged by the government's continued emphasis on infrastructure development, public transport connectivity, energy security and the transition towards a greener economy.
"We believe the 2027 Budget strikes a positive balance between addressing the immediate needs of Malaysians and laying the foundation for long-term economic competitiveness," he said.
He added that Mah Sing remained committed to supporting the government's aspirations by making quality homes more accessible, creating sustainable and liveable communities, and contributing to Malaysia's continued economic progress.
Leong said the group particularly welcomed the proposed extension and expansion of stamp duty exemptions for first-time homebuyers.
Eligible first-time buyers purchasing properties priced at up to RM500,000 currently enjoy full stamp duty exemptions on loan agreements and instruments of transfer under the Budget 2026 extension, covering sale and purchase agreements executed from Jan 1, 2026, to Dec 31, 2027.
"We welcome the 2027 Budget's proposed further extension of this relief to Dec 31, 2030," Leong said.
Mah Sing also welcomed the proposed expansion of stamp duty relief to eligible first-home purchases priced above RM500,000 and up to RM750,000.
Under the proposed measure, buyers would receive a full exemption on the first RM500,000 and a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount. The expanded relief would apply to sale and purchase agreements executed from Jan 1, 2027, to Dec 31, 2030.
Leong also lauded the government's increased allocation of RM16 billion for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programmes, alongside measures to improve access to affordable daily necessities.
He said the initiatives would provide meaningful support to households, particularly lower-income families, in managing their everyday expenses.
"Together with the proposed personal income tax relief measures, they reflect the government's commitment to easing the rakyat's financial burden and ensuring that the benefits of economic progress are more widely shared," he said.
Leong also welcomed the government's provision of up to RM20 billion in housing financing guarantees under the Skim Jaminan Kredit Perumahan, which aims to assist 80,000 first-time homebuyers, particularly self-employed individuals and those without fixed incomes.
He said the initiative would improve access to financing, enabling more Malaysians to take their first step towards homeownership and supporting a more inclusive housing market.
Additionally, Leong supported the stamp duty exemptions introduced to facilitate the revival of abandoned housing projects, in line with the government's target of eliminating abandoned housing projects by 2030.
"This initiative reflects the government's commitment to protecting homebuyers' interests, facilitating project rehabilitation, and strengthening confidence in the property industry."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lam Thye: Ensure swift compensation for accident victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Victims of accidents caused by drunk or drug-impaired drivers should receive fair compensation without having to endure lengthy court proceedings, says Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye.
He welcomed the government's proposal to amend the Road Transport Act to make compensation mandatory for victims of accidents involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs.
Lee said the proposal was justified as those responsible for causing accidents must be held accountable for the suffering and losses inflicted on their victims.
"We cannot allow these people to cause accidents and leave the victims to bear the consequences. Who is going to compensate them?" he said when contacted.
However, Lee said the government must establish a clear mechanism to determine the amount of compensation payable to victims.
He said compensation should take into account not only hospitalisation expenses but also loss of income and the financial impact on families who depended on the victims.
"When the government comes out with the law, it is very important that the compensation amount is fair.
"There must be a mechanism where these cases can be assessed and the amount of compensation determined by a designated body," he said.
He said victims should not have to rely solely on civil lawsuits to obtain compensation, as court proceedings could be costly and time-consuming.
"If victims have to take their cases to court and appoint lawyers, it will take a long time.
"I hope there will be a mechanism to ensure that compensation can be paid to victims quickly," he added.
Meanwhile, the Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) called for consistent enforcement against dangerous driving, including offences involving alcohol and drugs.
The consumer group welcomed initiatives under the 2027 Budget to improve road infrastructure, strengthen road safety and provide better protection for accident victims.
"Enforcement against dangerous driving, including driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, must be consistent.
"The government must also ensure that commercial vehicles and school transport services comply with safety requirements.
"Accident victims should have access to fair compensation and efficient claims procedures," it said in a statement.
The reactions followed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement that the government would amend the
Road Transport Act
to require drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate accident victims.
Anwar said 28 fatal cases involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs had been recorded as of August this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MEF: June 2027 wage hike gives businesses breathing room
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed the decision to give employers until June 2027 to prepare for the minimum wage increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month.
MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Dr Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the transition period would give businesses time to plan while minimising disruption to employment and operations.
He said a reasonable adjustment period, coupled with support for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), would help improve workers' incomes without undermining business sustainability and job security.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the increase when tabling 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today, saying it would benefit more than four million workers.
Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy must consider not only higher salaries but also businesses' ability to sustain wage increases, retain existing workers and create new jobs.
"For employers, a wage increase is not simply an adjustment to basic salary. It also affects statutory contributions, overtime payments and other employment-related costs.
"For businesses operating on narrow margins, these additional costs can significantly affect their ability to sustain operations and retain employees," he said in a statement.
He said MSMEs faced greater constraints than larger businesses in absorbing higher labour costs, amid rising operating expenses, limited access to financing, productivity gaps and challenges in adopting technology.
An exemption for eligible MSMEs with annual sales below RM50 million would give them greater flexibility to strengthen their finances, improve productivity and prepare for future wage adjustments without jeopardising jobs, he added.
"We must ensure that higher wages translate into better livelihoods, not fewer job opportunities," he said, adding that sustainable wage growth must allow businesses to remain competitive, continue hiring and invest in productivity.
MEF urged the government to establish clear eligibility criteria and transparent guidelines for the RM50 million annual sales threshold, including the relevant financial year, treatment of related entities and applicability to different business structures.
It also proposed complementary measures, including targeted productivity incentives, digitalisation and automation support, skills development and cost-reduction initiatives for MSMEs.
"Sustainable wage growth cannot depend on wage increases alone. It must be supported by higher productivity, stronger business performance and a more competitive economy," he said.
Syed Hussain added that MEF supported Anwar's call for employers that could afford to do so to pay above the statutory minimum wage.
"While the minimum wage establishes the statutory floor, it should not be the ceiling for employers who can afford to pay more. MEF encourages employers to reward staff in line with business performance, productivity and skill," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Azalina: Law Reform Commission to address gaps in legal framework
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's proposal to establish a Malaysian Law Reform Commission will pave the way for a comprehensive review of outdated laws and gaps in the country's legal framework.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said in welcoming the announcement under the
2027 Budget
, said it was a reflection of the government's continued commitment to legal and institutional reforms.
She said the proposed commission would help identify outdated legislation, address gaps in existing laws and modernise legislation governing contracts, the sale of goods and mediation.
"This initiative demonstrates the government's determination to implement comprehensive and continuous legal reforms, including identifying outdated laws, addressing legislative gaps and modernising laws relating to contracts, the sale of goods and mediation," she said in a statement today.
She also reaffirmed the government's commitment to separating the roles of the Attorney-General (A-G) and public prosecutor, although the proposal remained under review.
She said institutional reforms required the government to be prepared to limit its own powers.
"The most meaningful reform is the courage of a government to limit its own powers.
"Although efforts to limit the prime minister's tenure have yet to secure a two-thirds majority in Parliament, while the separation of the A-G and public prosecutor roles is still under review, the government's determination to pursue these reforms remains firm while respecting the parliamentary democratic process," she said.
Meanwhile, the government's decision to increase the bankruptcy threshold from RM100,000 to RM150,000 formed part of three initiatives under the 2027 Budget to strengthen the Second Chance Policy, she said.
She said this was following efforts that had helped more than 250,000 people emerge from bankruptcy since 2023.
The other measures include expanding the Second Chance Policy to primary caregivers of family members with disabilities, chronic patients and senior citizens, as well as gig workers and people with irregular incomes.
The government will also strengthen the automatic discharge mechanism under Section 33C of the Insolvency Act, allowing eligible bankrupt individuals to be discharged as early as three years.
On a separate matter, Azalina said the expansion of individual lifestyle tax relief to cover vaccination costs and the adoption of pets from registered centres would encourage responsible pet ownership.
As Pengerang MP, Azalina also welcomed Petronas' full ownership of the Pengerang Integrated Complex, which she said would strengthen the country's fuel supply security.
She said the development of the Pengerang Biorefinery in collaboration with Enilive, Eni and Euglena to produce low-carbon fuels would create economic opportunities and high-value jobs.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze disrupts routines, leaves parents scrambling for childcare
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Worsening haze has disrupted daily routines, raised safety concerns among road users and forced parents to scramble for childcare arrangements following the short-notice announcement of school closures.
While some have reported health concerns and cut back on outdoor activities, others are urging employers to consider work-from-home (WFH) arrangements to reduce exposure to the haze.
Grab rider Ravi Chandraan said he had been unwell for the past three days, which he attributed to the haze.
He said poor visibility on the roads had also made riding his motorcycle more difficult, raising concerns about safety while working.
Meanwhile, Nurul Adillah, who works in Cyberjaya, said she had stopped her usual outdoor activities as the haze worsened.
"Usually, I would go jogging, hiking or do other outdoor activities during the weekend. However, with the haze getting worse, I have to stay at home and spend less time outdoors," she said.
The situation has also affected parents following the announcement of school closures at short notice.
Mother of two, Nazatul Shima said she struggled to make alternative arrangements for her children after learning about the closure late last night.
"Not every parent has a backup plan or family members living nearby who can help take care of their children," she said.
She hoped employers would be understanding of parents facing difficulties managing childcare arrangements amid the sudden changes.
Sujitraaa Sugumaran said employers should consider implementing full WFH arrangements in view of the current situation.
"Health is more important than anything, and it is getting scarier to go outside, especially with the risks to our health," she said.
For commuters, exposure to the haze remains a concern even during their daily journeys to public transport stations.
Poja Conie Mila Charlie said she had to walk through the haze every morning from her home to the nearest LRT station.
She said visibility along the road was poor, making her daily commute more concerning.
Conie also recounted seeing seven students at the Johan Setia LRT station this morning who were returning home after being misinformed about the school closure announced last night.
The situation remains concerning, with 37 areas recording
unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings
today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PNB gets first new land endowment in over 40 years
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget will strengthen Permodalan Nasional Bhd's (PNB) mandate to grow Bumiputera wealth through a new endowment of 20.23 hectares of prime commercial land in Kuala Lumpur.
PNB president and group chief executive Datuk Rizal Rickman Ramli said the allocation marks the group's first new endowment since its formative years in the early 1980s.
He said it reinforces PNB's founding mandate to enhance Bumiputera wealth and participation through long-term value creation.
"The new endowment reflects a long-term commitment to preserving strategic Bumiputera ownership, unlocking sustainable economic value from national assets, and ensuring the benefits generated can continue to grow and serve future generations," he said in a statement.
Rizal said PNB would maximise the land's economic potential by preserving and reinvesting the underlying capital to support future growth, while distributing profits to its unitholders.
He also welcomed the government's recognition of PNB's role in preserving Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, as well as the entertainment duty exemption for arts, cultural, entertainment and sporting activities held at both venues.
"This initiative will encourage greater public participation and utilisation of these historic landmarks, while supporting ongoing efforts to revitalise and preserve Malaysia's national heritage at Merdeka 118 Precinct," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tax relief could ease M40 burden, says consumer group
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A prominent consumer group said 2027 Budget tax relief measures could ease the financial pressure on middle-income households amid rising living costs.
Federation of Malaysian Consumers Associations (Fomca) chief executive officer Dr T. Saravanan said the increase in individual income tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000, alongside proposed tax rate reductions and wider deductions, would help M40 households manage their expenses.
He said the changes recognised the financial pressures faced by M40 families, whose commitments often included housing loans or rental payments, vehicle instalments, childcare, school expenses, healthcare, medical insurance premiums and the cost of caring for elderly parents.
"Although these households may earn above the B40 income threshold, their disposable income after meeting essential commitments could remain limited," he said.
The additional tax relief would allow eligible taxpayers to retain more of their income, giving them some breathing room in managing household expenditure.
The basic
individual tax relief will increase
to RM12,000 from RM9,000, marking the first revision to the limit since 2010.
However, Fomca cautioned that tax relief alone would not fully address the financial challenges faced by the M40. It called on the government to ensure public healthcare, education, childcare and public transport remained affordable and accessible.
"The government must provide clear information and practical examples explaining how the revised tax relief and rates would benefit taxpayers across different income levels.
"It is equally important to recognise that individuals who do not pay income tax, or whose tax liability is already low, may receive little or no direct benefit from these changes," Saravanan said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced that individual income tax relief would increase to RM12,000 from RM9,000, while tax rates for those with taxable incomes of RM70,000 to RM100,000 and RM100,000 to RM150,000 would be reduced by one percentage point to 18 and 24 per cent respectively.
Fomca also welcomed the increase in allocations for the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) programmes to RM16 billion next year, from RM15 billion this year.
Saravanan described the RM1 billion increase as a timely measure amid cost-of-living pressures.
STR and Sara are designed to
ease Malaysians' daily expenses
while the government continues to implement reforms and strengthen the economy to raise incomes and improve living standards. The goal is not just to provide aid, but to improve people's lives.
He said the monthly Sara assistance of up to RM150 for eligible STR recipients would help families manage daily expenses, particularly food and other essential household items.
The group also backed the RM100 assistance for Malaysians aged 18 and above who were not STR recipients, which is scheduled to be distributed twice next year.
Anwar said the payments would be made ahead of Hari Raya Aidilfitri and in conjunction with the country's 70th Merdeka celebrations.
Saravanan cautioned that the adequacy of the assistance must be assessed against the actual cost of living. Additional aid of RM50 or RM100 might provide only temporary relief as households continued to face rising expenses for food, housing, transport, healthcare and children's education.
He said the government should look beyond income classifications when determining eligibility, as many M40 households, particularly those in urban areas with several dependants, were also facing significant financial pressure.
"Most importantly, the government must strengthen price monitoring and enforcement. There is little benefit in increasing financial assistance if traders subsequently raise prices and the additional assistance is absorbed by higher living costs.
"We must also ensure there are no leakages, that eligible recipients are not left out, and that Sara-approved products remain readily available at reasonable prices, including in rural areas."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Four injured as 10-tonne lorry hits vehicles in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Four people were injured, including a man who sustained critical head injuries, when a 10-tonne lorry travelling against the flow of traffic rammed into vehicles in the opposite lane at the Alam Budiman traffic lights along Jalan Mokhtar Dahari today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the victims comprised three men and a woman.
"One of the men was trapped and sustained critical head injuries, while another man suffered abdominal injuries. A third man sustained minor injuries, while the woman suffered moderately critical head injuries.
"All four victims were successfully extricated and handed over to Health Ministry personnel for treatment," he said in a statement.
He said the department received an emergency call at 4.31pm, and a fire engine from the Bukit Jelutong fire and rescue station arrived at the scene at 4.47pm.
Five firefighters and one fire and rescue tender were deployed to the scene.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral, showing a tipper lorry travelling against the flow of traffic and hitting vehicles in the opposite lane at a junction.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget gives MoH room to push reforms, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's move to offer 9,000 permanent posts to contract doctors is a positive step towards addressing the country's doctor shortage.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the implementation of permanent appointments would take time, as the ministry needed to ensure candidates met the requirements and take into account the different batches and cohorts of medical officers.
"We will implement this innovatively so that it can be addressed as soon as possible.
"We will put an end to the interim contract system," he said on the sidelines of the 2027 Budget announcement today.
He said his ministry was working with the Higher Education Ministry, Public Service Department and Public Services Commission to address workforce issues more holistically.
"Previously, the approach was rather fragmented, from workforce supply and deployment to specialisation and other matters.
"Today, we have reorganised these elements into an integrated and seamless approach, rather than having them operate separately as before," he said.
On the Flying Doctor Service's (FDS) allowance, Dzulkefly said the ministry would continue strengthening healthcare access through land, air and river transport, particularly for people in remote areas.
Asked whether the ministry planned to own helicopters for the FDS, he said the ministry's priority was providing healthcare services rather than operating helicopters.
"We are not in the business of operating helicopters. We are in the business of providing services. Our responsibility is to safeguard the people's health and provide them with treatment.
"For such matters, we favour a leasing approach. It is easier and more effective, and does not burden us with the responsibility of operating and maintaining the helicopters," he said.
While tabling the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government
will offer permanent positions
to more than 9,000 contract doctors in 2027, as it moves to resolve the long-standing issue of contract medical officers.
Anwar said the government had appointed more than 15,000 contract doctors to permanent positions since 2023, including 4,000 this year.
In a separate announcement, Anwar said the monthly post-basic incentive for 47,000 paramedics and nurses would be increased from RM100 to RM200.
This follows an increase in the Health Ministry's allocation to RM47.7 billion next year, from RM46.5 billion this year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: MCMC to invest RM1bil in electronic medical records
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will invest RM1 billion to expand the Electronic Medical Record System to healthcare facilities nationwide.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said during the tabling of 2027 Budget that the government would introduce the MediAsas basic medical plan in January 2027 at an affordable premium.
"Under this plan, hospital charges will be based on the type of diagnosis and treatment to ensure costs are more controlled and predictable," he said.
Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members below 55 will be allowed to pay MediAsas premiums through their Akaun Sejahtera.
The government will also subsidise RM200 of the first-year premium for each employee at small and medium enterprises (SMEs) with fewer than 75 employees. The subsidy will be capped at 50 employees per company.
The initiative is expected to benefit up to 200,000 workers, Anwar said.
Meanwhile, electronic medical records will be expanded based on the principle of "one individual, one record" to improve transparency in private healthcare costs.
From 2027, private hospital bills will use standardised and transparent charge categories to help patients understand each payment and reduce price distortions, he said.
The upcoming e-CKAPS portal will also enable private healthcare facility licensing to be conducted entirely online from 2027. Processing times are expected to be reduced by up to 65 per cent.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM450mil opportunity for startups from Khazanah, KWAP - Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khazanah's Jelawang Capital and the Retirement Fund (Incorporated) (KWAP) Pioneer Fund will invest RM450 million in start-up developments.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the New Industrial Master Plan (NIMP) Fund, KWAP's Dana Pemacu, and Khazanah's Malaysia Mid-Tier Companies (MTC) Fund - totalling RM2.1 billion - will also be utilised to strengthen mid-tier companies' capabilities in sectors such as electrical and electronics, digital, aerospace, and medical devices.
"To attract private capital through equity crowdfunding (ECF) and peer-to-peer (P2P) platforms, RM270 million has been allocated to support small and medium enterprises (SMEs), mid-tier companies, and social enterprises.
"Income tax exemptions for individual investors on ECF platforms, and for angel investors funding early-stage technology start-ups, will be extended to Dec 31, 2030," he said when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, announced a RM41 million allocation to Cradle Fund to implement the Start-up Ecosystem Roadmap and provide grants for prototype development and commercialisation.
The fifth Madani Budget, themed "Malaysia Madani: Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi," is the second budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: RM5bil to strengthen internet connectivity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will allocate RM5 billion to strengthen the country's internet connectivity through the Jendela project.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said WiFi coverage had been provided at all public university campuses, while 4G coverage had been extended to all Felda settlements.
"We have so far successfully provided WiFi coverage at all public university campuses and 4G coverage in all Felda settlements," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget.
He said efforts next year would also focus on ensuring internet connectivity along 7,000km of roads and 1,700km of railway lines, as well as implementing the Madani Submarine Cable (Salam) project.
Separately, the government will focus on extending 4G coverage to all Orang Asli villages.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MARC: 2027 Budget balances growth with fiscal discipline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget reflects the government's sustained commitment to support economic growth while advancing fiscal consolidation, said Malaysian Rating Corp Bhd (MARC).
Group chief executive officer Arshad Mohamed Ismail said the narrowing of the fiscal deficit, alongside sustained development expenditure, provides a foundation for strengthening Malaysia's economic resilience and long-term growth potential.
"The reduction in the fiscal deficit to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 reinforces the government's commitment to remain on the fiscal consolidation path," he said in a statement.
He also welcomed the higher allocation for development expenditure at RM83 billion.
"Continued investment can help strengthen Malaysia's productive capacity while also creating opportunities for greater private sector participation.
"The focus should therefore not only be on the size of the allocation but also on the quality and effectiveness of spending and its ability to generate longer-term economic returns," he added.
Additionally, he said the gradual shift towards a broader, more sustainable revenue base should help strengthen Malaysia's fiscal position over time.
"Continued efforts to broaden revenue sources, improve the efficiency of targeted subsidies and enhance the quality of public spending will further reinforce the fiscal position, while ensuring that resources remain available for strategic investments and national development priorities," he added.
The government has projected total spending and investments of RM510 billion under the 2027 budget, up from RM470 billion this year, while targeting a lower fiscal deficit of 3.3 per cent of GDP.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the allocation comprises RM376.8 billion in federal operating expenditure and RM83 billion in development expenditure.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Govt allocates RM142mil to boost Nadi platform, online business
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will allocate RM142 million under 2027 Budget to strengthen the National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) platform and help more young entrepreneurs grow their businesses online.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the initiative would enable more entrepreneurs to tap into digital business opportunities and reach wider markets.
He cited the example of Azmi Warisan, a coffee entrepreneur from Kampung Sungai Leman, Selangor, who used the Nadi platform to expand his business.
The platform helped Azmi increase his sales by 80 per cent to RM240,000.
The additional allocation is intended to help more entrepreneurs use digital platforms to promote their products, expand their customer base and grow their businesses.
The initiative is part of the government's efforts to strengthen digital entrepreneurship and create more opportunities for local businesses.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Faster licensing to boost medical tourism, says APHM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Faster licensing of private healthcare facilities under a new online system could give Malaysia's medical tourism sector a boost, the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) said.
Its president, Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh, said the development of the e-CKAPS portal, which will enable private healthcare facility licensing to be conducted entirely online from next year, is expected to reduce processing times by up to 65 per cent.
He said the initiative was among the healthcare measures welcomed by APHM in the 2027 Budget, alongside efforts to strengthen public-private collaboration and improve patients' access to treatment.
"Faster licensing will cut waiting times for approvals and give a welcome boost to Malaysia's medical tourism sector," he said in a statement.
Kuljit also welcomed the increase in the allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals to RM200 million, as well as more flexible sessional arrangements for private-sector specialists, with the maximum engagement period extended.
He said the measures could help reduce patient waiting times by making better use of private-sector healthcare capacity.
APHM had also worked closely with the government to improve billing transparency, ensuring patients had a clearer understanding of the charges they incurred.
"We are pleased to see this reflected in the 2027 Budget and look forward to further discussions with all stakeholders on its implementation to ensure the best outcome for patients," he said.
Kuljit said the effectiveness of the initiatives should ultimately be measured by their impact on patients rather than the size of the budget increase.
"What matters most is not the size of the budget increase but the outcome for patients.
"APHM stands ready to work closely with the Health Ministry and other stakeholders to turn these measures into real improvements on the ground," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the 2027 Budget announced that the Health Ministry's allocation will increase to RM47.7 billion from RM46.5 billion next year.
Anwar also said the government would resolve the contract doctor issue, adding that more than 15,000 contract doctors had been appointed to permanent positions since 2023, including 4,000 this year.
Next year, more than 9,000 contract doctors will be offered permanent positions, with those who successfully complete their housemanship subsequently offered permanent medical officer posts, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang welcomes 2027 Budget backing for proposed tech finance hub
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Penang has welcomed the federal government's backing for its proposed Penang Technology Financial Centre (PTFC), saying the move would strengthen the state's technology ecosystem and support its push towards higher-value industries.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the recognition was a positive development, particularly for the electrical and electronics (E&E) and semiconductor sectors.
He said the initiative would help Malaysia move towards a high-value, technology-driven economy while creating opportunities to strengthen local industries.
"The state government submitted the PTFC White Paper to the Finance Ministry on Sept 23, and plans to submit the PTFC Strategic Blueprint and PTFC Action Plan by November," he said.
The documents would outline the initiative's direction, implementation strategies and measures needed to establish the proposed hub.
In his 2027 Budget speech, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced plans to develop Penang as a national technology hub, supported by a RM100 million
fund
established by Khazanah Nasional Bhd and InvestPenang for early-stage semiconductor and advanced manufacturing companies.
Following the announcement, Chow said the state would continue discussions with the Finance Ministry on establishing a federal-state joint committee to coordinate planning, implementation and follow-up action.
He said the PTFC was aligned with the National Semiconductor Strategy, which aims to strengthen Malaysia's position in the global semiconductor value chain and develop domestic technological capabilities.
Chow said the initiative could deliver three key economic benefits: strengthening local manufacturing linked to the E&E and semiconductor industries, moving Penang towards higher-value economic activities, and building Malaysia's intellectual property (IP) and technological capabilities.
"The initiative will also expand opportunities in advanced technology, innovation and knowledge-based industries, including hard technology and deep technology, supporting the country's ambition to develop products and technologies under the 'Made by Malaysia' vision.
"The state government will continue working closely with the federal government to translate the PTFC initiative into new economic opportunities, stronger local industries and improved Malaysian competitiveness in the global technology landscape," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Prasarana to invest RM3.4bil in rail recovery programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prasarana Malaysia Bhd will invest RM3.4 billion in a rail service recovery programme to improve service reliability, operational efficiency and passenger experience under the 2027 Budget.
In a statement, the public transport operator welcomed the measures announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, which emphasised accessibility, service reliability and passenger comfort.
Prasarana said the investment formed part of its long-term commitment to strengthening rail system capacity and resilience, optimising asset performance and minimising service disruptions.
"Prasarana expresses its appreciation to the government for its decision to continue the My50 travel pass, which benefits approximately 300,000 users of rail and bus services operated by Rapid KL in the Klang Valley every month," said Prasarana.
It added that the continuation of the initiative was important in helping ease the cost of living, particularly for those who rely on public transport for their daily commute.
Prasarana also acknowledged the government's emphasis on ensuring smoother rail operations to improve passenger convenience and comfort.
The company said it was committed to improving operational efficiency, strengthening maintenance and addressing technical issues comprehensively to ensure stable, safe and reliable services.
"As the country's largest public transport service provider, Prasarana will continue to fulfil its responsibility to provide a safe, efficient, inclusive and sustainable mobility system, while supporting the national aspiration of achieving a 40 per cent public transport modal share by 2030," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Taxi, hire car and school bus drivers to get RM1,000 aid next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Taxi, hire car and school bus drivers will receive a one-off RM1,000 financial aid following the sale of the special "H" number plate series, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced.
He said the aid would benefit 38,000 taxi and hire car drivers and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide, with payments to be disbursed next week.
"Following the recent sale of the special 'H' number plates, the government has agreed to give a one-off special financial aid of RM1,000 to 38,000 taxi drivers, including hire cars, and 15,000 school bus drivers nationwide," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
Anwar said proceeds from the sale of the special number plates had been channelled back to the people through various initiatives.
"For example, proceeds from the sale of special number plates have been returned to the people," he said.
He said university students had received RM500 in flight ticket aid, while youths from poor backgrounds could take the B2 motorcycle licence test for free. Free helmets had also been distributed.
The Road Transport Department (RTD) raised
RM91.2 million
from the "H" series, which was auctioned online from Sept 16 to 20 in conjunction with Malaysia Day.
The "H1" plate fetched a record
RM10.78 million.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: One-off RM1,500 special aid for 1.3 million civil servants
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has announced a one-off special financial assistance payment of RM1,500 for 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including contract workers.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said all government pensioners, including pensioned and non-pensioned veterans, would also receive RM750 in special financial assistance.
"The payments will be made on two occasions, before Aidilfitri and in conjunction with the 70th Merdeka anniversary," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget at the Dewan Rakyat here today.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had agreed to provide a one-off special payment of RM750 to 70,000 KAFA religious teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks and other Islamic religious personnel.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Saifuddin: 2027 Budget prioritises public safety, national sovereignty
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The RM21.98 billion allocation to the Home Ministry under the 2027 Budget will strengthen security assets, border controls and technology to combat crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the allocation reflected the Madani government's commitment to safeguarding peace and public order, which he described as fundamental to national prosperity.
"The allocation for the Home Ministry of RM21,982,691,300 reflects the Madani government's firm resolve that peace and public order remain a priority.
"Allocations for welfare, stronger security assets, enhanced border control and the use of technology to combat crime showed that public safety and national sovereignty could not be compromised.
"A peaceful nation gives the people confidence to go about their daily lives, while creating a conducive environment for business, investment and tourism," he said in a statement.
Saifuddin said public welfare remained a priority, with investments in healthcare facilities, public transport assistance, skills development and employment opportunities.
He said the true measure of a Budget's success was not merely the amount allocated, but how effectively it eased the cost of living and improved the well-being of Malaysian families.
On the economy, Saifuddin said the country's growth, trade and investment performance must translate into more quality jobs, higher incomes, business opportunities and a more manageable cost of living.
He said public welfare, security and economic strength were interconnected, adding that economic growth must deliver tangible benefits to the people.
"The challenge ahead is to ensure that every allocation is implemented efficiently, transparently and effectively so that its benefits truly reach the people," he said.
Earlier, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said under the
2027 Budget, the Home Ministry and Defence Ministry
will each receive RM22 billion, with RM7.1 billion allocated for the purchase and maintenance of assets for the armed forces, police and uniformed agencies under the Home Ministry.
The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency will receive RM490 million, while 48 new body and baggage scanners will be installed at KLIA, Penang and Kota Kinabalu airports.
The National Scam Response Centre will develop an AI-powered application to check suspicious phone numbers, bank accounts and links, while police will enhance the Malaysia Internet Crime Against Children system to detect perpetrators and child sexual exploitation networks earlier.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pasir Gudang tops nationwide API readings as 36 areas record unhealthy air
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: Johor's Pasir Gudang recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 190 as of 5pm today, with 35 other areas nationwide also registering unhealthy levels.
In Johor, Segamat recorded 187, followed by Larkin (185), Tangkak (183), Batu Pahat (177), Kluang (176), Pengerang (175), and Kota Tinggi (175).
Melaka's Bukit Rambai recorded 187, followed by Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181).
In Negri Sembilan, Seremban recorded 189, followed by Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174).
Perak's Tasek Ipoh recorded 182, followed by Pegoh Ipoh (176) and Tanjung Malim (174).
Selangor's Johan Setia recorded 181, followed by Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (167), Klang (167), Banting (166), and Kuala Selangor (156).
In Kuala Lumpur, Cheras recorded 177 and Batu Muda 172, while Putrajaya recorded 170.
Meanwhile, 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate readings.
In the East Coast, Terengganu's Kemaman recorded 98, followed by Besut (88), Paka (87), and Kuala Terengganu (66).
Pahang recorded 156 in Temerloh, 79 in Balok Baru Kuantan, 74 in Jerantut, and 71 in Indera Mahkota Kuantan.
Kelantan recorded 89 in Kota Baru and 84 in Tanah Merah.
Up north, Penang's Balik Pulau recorded 89, Kedah's Kulim Hi-Tech recorded 85, Langkawi recorded 73, and Perlis' Kangar recorded 81.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 158 and Taiping 110.
Sarawak recorded moderate readings in Kuching (88), Serian (85), Sri Aman (83), Samarahan (82), Bintulu (76), Samalaju (76), Mukah (72), Miri (71), Sarikei (71), Sibu (69), Kapit (68), ILP Miri (65), and Limbang (59).
Sabah recorded moderate readings in Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (61), Keningau (60), Kimanis (59), Kota Kinabalu (59), Sandakan (55), and Tawau (54), while Labuan recorded 63.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and 301 and above hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Govt to disclose project contractors, contract values for transparency
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will strengthen transparency by disclosing project information, including contractors and contract values, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
"With the Government Procurement Act coming into force in 2027, the government will strengthen transparency by disclosing project details, including contractors' names and contract values," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
Anwar said the Madani reform agenda would continue to be strengthened "without fear" as the administration entered its fifth year.
He said a bill on government-owned entities would be tabled to tighten governance of entities entrusted with managing public money and assets.
The bill would cover government companies and statutory bodies, to prevent scandals such as 1MDB, the Tabung Haji crisis and Felda from recurring.
Anwar said all loan repayments collected by federal statutory bodies, including education and business loans funded through operating and development allocations, must be reused only for approved purposes and target groups. This would also cover interest earned from the funds.
Meanwhile, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), police, the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Customs Department and the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) would receive RM1.1 billion to strengthen their operational capabilities.
The government is also studying the setting up of a Malaysian Law Reform Commission to identify outdated laws and legal gaps, he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar brings poetry to 2027 Budget with Tamil, Chinese verses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Classical Tamil and Chinese poetry featured in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's 2027 Budget speech in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, an avid reader of poetry, literature and political philosophy, including the works of Rumi, drew on the literary traditions of two ancient civilisations in his speech.
When announcing allocations for the Health Ministry, he quoted verse 731 from Tirukkural, the celebrated work of revered Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar.
Reciting the verse, Anwar said: "Thallaa Vilaiyulum Thakkaarum Thaazhvilaach Chelvarum Servadhu Naadu."
He said the verse described an ideal nation as one blessed with fertile land, knowledgeable people of good character and prosperity that did not come at the expense of moral values.
Anwar also drew on classical Chinese poetry when outlining the eighth pillar of the Budget, which focuses on managing public funds with integrity.
Quoting a renowned poet from the Tang dynasty, he recited a line from Shangtang Kaishi Song.
The Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907 and is widely regarded as a golden age of Chinese poetry, producing celebrated poets and works that continue to influence Chinese literature.
Anwar recited: "Bù jīng yī fān hán chè gǔ, zěn dé méi huā pū bí xiāng."
The saying means that the fragrance of the plum blossom cannot emerge without first enduring cold that bites to the bone.
In Malay, he rendered it as: "Tidak akan terbit keharuman bunga plum tanpa terlebih dahulu mengharungi dingin yang menggigit hingga ke tulang."
Anwar said the metaphor reflected a truth about life and human struggle.
"Great achievements do not come from prolonged comfort, but require perseverance, patience and a willingness to endure hardship," he said.
The government has allocated RM459.84 billion for Budget 2027, with spending covering public-sector salaries, subsidies, debt servicing and economic development, Anwar said earlier.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Permanent posts for contract doctors will help stem brain drain, says APHM
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Offering permanent posts to doctors who complete their housemanship will help stem the brain drain and strengthen the country's healthcare workforce, said Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh.
He said the move would give young doctors greater job security and clearer career prospects, encouraging them to build their careers in Malaysia instead of seeking better opportunities and stability abroad.
"I am glad that the contract doctor issue is resolved and commend the government on offering permanent posts to doctors who complete their housemanship. This will give young doctors the job security and career prospects they deserve.
"It also helps address the brain drain, as too many of our talented doctors have been lured abroad by better prospects and greater stability.
"Keeping them here means a stronger, more stable healthcare workforce for the nation," he said in a statement.
Kuljit said a stronger domestic healthcare workforce could improve hospital staffing levels and potentially reduce waiting times for consultations and treatment.
He added that the measures, coupled with greater public-private collaboration, would help ensure Malaysians received timely, quality healthcare.
The Health Ministry's allocation will increase to RM47.7 billion from RM46.5 billion next year through the 2027 Budget.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the Budget said the government would address the contract doctor issue, adding that more than 15,000 contract doctors had been appointed to permanent positions since 2023, including 4,000 this year.
More than 9,000 contract doctors
will be offered permanent positions next year, with those who successfully complete their housemanship subsequently offered permanent medical officer posts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Parents, students adapt to online learning as schools close
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prior experience with Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) has enabled parents and students to adapt smoothly as schools in several states closed due to haze.
Teachers' prompt preparation of digital learning materials and assignments ensured uninterrupted education, allowing students to keep up with lessons and exam preparations at home.
In the federal capital, civil servant Marlina, 44, said her afternoon work shift allowed her to guide her 8-year-old daughter, a Year Two pupil at SK Danau Kota 2, during morning online sessions.
"My daughter was eager to attend school, but I explained that physical classes were suspended due to the haze and lessons would continue online. Fortunately, she is accustomed to online learning, having experienced it in kindergarten during the Covid-19 pandemic," she said.
She praised teachers for quickly issuing assignment links and materials despite late-night closure announcements, making home instruction manageable for parents.
In Selangor, Razif Mat Arbak, 42, said home-based learning alleviated health concerns for his son, an SPM candidate at SMK Tinggi Klang, while allowing uninterrupted preparation for examinations scheduled later this month.
"At least he can learn via PdPR and focus on materials provided by teachers without braving the outdoors, which is becoming increasingly concerning," he said.
Raheemie Arifin, 39, whose Year Three child attends SK Taman Tun Dr Ismail Jaya in Shah Alam, backed the Education Ministry's decision to close primary schools, noting younger children are more vulnerable to air pollution risks.
In Negri Sembilan, students similarly used online platforms to prepare for upcoming tests.
Form Two student Dania Irdina Mohd Hair Adnan, 14, of SMK Seremban 3, said teachers posted assignments on Google Classroom as early as 7.45am, with submissions made through their Digital Educational Learning Initiative Malaysia (DELIMa) 3.0 accounts.
"With end-of-year examinations scheduled next week, missing classes would mean losing valuable revision tips and sample questions," she said.
In Johor, frontline worker Muhammad Faiz Husin, 36, said past experience helped parents manage home study more systematically, though continuous supervision remains necessary to meet submission deadlines.
In Melaka, implementation varied by school, with some teachers conducting live streams while others assigned exercises via messaging platforms.
Asmawati Ibrahim, 37, from Semabok, said her Year Three child began lessons at 8am following the standard timetable for English, Islamic Education, Mathematics, and Science.
She said despite receiving instructions late at night, parents had sufficient time to prepare printing materials and access interactive quizzes.
Amyleena Ashakri, 30, whose Year One child attends school in Tengkera, added that teachers shared exercises through
class WhatsApp groups
for parents to facilitate at home.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said in a statement yesterday that schools in four states, including one district in Pahang, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya will be closed today following the worsening haze situation.
The closures involve all schools in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, as well as schools in Rompin, Pahang.
Today, Perak Education Department director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar announced the
closures
of all Education Ministry schools and educational institutions in Kinta Utara, Kinta Selatan and Kuala Kangsar.S
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Govt mulls commission to overhaul outdated laws
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is studying a proposal to establish a Malaysian Law Reform Commission to review outdated laws and identify gaps in the country's legal framework.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government was also reviewing laws on contracts, the sale of goods and mediation to expedite the resolution of legal disputes.
"The government is studying the establishment of a Malaysian Law Reform Commission to identify outdated laws and gaps in the legal framework.
"Laws relating to contracts, the sale of goods and mediation are also being reviewed to ensure disputes can be resolved more quickly," he said when tabling the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said reforms to criminal and evidence laws would also be undertaken, alongside efforts to strengthen public defence services and improve protection for victims, children and vulnerable groups.
"Criminal and evidence laws will be reformed, public defence strengthened, and victims, children and vulnerable groups given more effective protection," he said.
He added that the Madani administration remained committed to institutional reforms as it entered its fifth year in power, with efforts focused on strengthening accountability and upholding the rule of law.
However, Anwar did not specify when the proposed commission would be established or which laws would be reviewed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 2027 Budget: Maternity leave up to 490 days, minimum pension RM1,350
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Maternity leave entitlement for civil servants will increase from 360 days to 490 days throughout their service, while the minimum monthly pension will rise from RM1,000 to RM1,350 under the 2027 Budget.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said maternity leave would be increased to a maximum of 98 days per childbirth, with RM20 million allocated to improve childcare centres at government facilities.
Meanwhile, he said the higher minimum pension would benefit nearly 59,000 retirees, armed forces veterans and derivative pension recipients.
Anwar also expressed his appreciation to the country's 1.6 million civil servants for their dedication to serving the nation, describing them as the driving force behind the Madani vision to elevate the country's standing, dignity and progress.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: One day to wedding, Syed Saddiq turns up for 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Most grooms spend the eve of their wedding making final preparations, but Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman had another date to keep today — attending Parliament.
Dressed in a black Baju Melayu, Syed Saddiq attended the Dewan Rakyat for the tabling of the 2027 Budget, a day before his wedding to singer-actress Bella Astillah tomorrow.
The couple got engaged on March 28 and will exchange vows at Menara Merdeka Maybank here.
Two days ago, Syed Saddiq had said that the couple had to put their
honeymoon
plans on ice for now.
He said, "Perhaps after getting married, we'll have our honeymoon in Parliament. I'm only joking, of course."
After tomorrow's wedding ceremony, the couple will host a reception for family and close friends on Oct 18.
They will also celebrate with the public through two "Kenduri Rakyat" receptions in Muar, Johor, on Oct 25, and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on Oct 31.
Bella, whose real name is Dayang Nabellah Awang Astillah, married Singaporean actor-singer Aliff Aziz in September 2016.
They share two children — 9-year-old Mohamed Ayden Adrean and 6-year-old Ara Adreanna — and divorced in May 2019 before briefly reconciling.
They finalised their second divorce on June 13, 2024.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sabah, with RM18.6b in allocations, hails 2027 budget as alleviating burden for all Malaysians
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 9 — Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor described the National 2027 Budget as a comprehensive budget that alleviates the people's financial burden and reflects the strength of the country's economy.
He said the budget that was proposed earlier today saw benefitted Malaysians through tax reductions and incentives for civil servants, businesses and all segments of society.
“It demonstrates the strength of our country's economy and financial position, despite the impact of the ongoing crisis in West Asia,” he said after watching the live broadcast of the tabling of the National 2027 Budget at Menara Kinabalu today.
In Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s proposed budget, Sabah continues to be the biggest recipient of federal allocations with RM18.6 billion for next year, an increase of 6.25 per cent compared to RM17.6 billion for this year.
In addition, Anwar said road projects in Sabah and Sarawak would continue with an allocation of RM3.3 billion under the 2027 Budget.
He also announced that the government had agreed to double the number of Public Service Department (JPA) scholarships offered to students from Sabah and Sarawak.
“This means that 4,200 students from Sabah and Sarawak will have the opportunity to pursue higher education at universities each year,” he said.
On boosting power supply system, he said the government has also agreed to install Static Synchronous Compensator (STATCOM) systems at the Dam Road and Segaliud Main Intake Substations at a cost of RM204 million.
The Southern Link Transmission Line project will also proceed as a long-term measure to ensure the sustainability of electricity supply in Sabah.
Road infrastructure along the borders of Sabah, Sarawak and Kalimantan will also continue to be upgraded to facilitate two-way movement.
Anwar also reiterated that the resolution of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) with the two east Malaysian state was to be viewed as part of the national covenant and promised that the interim payment of RM1.5 billion will be settled before the end of the year, while negotiations with Sabah and Sarawak will continue to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.
Also watching the live telecast with Hajiji were Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun, State Secretary Datuk Zainudin Aman, assistant ministers and senior state government officers.

Title: Lim Guan Eng calls Budget 2027 Anwar’s ‘most reform-minded’ yet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng today described Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth Madani Budget as the “most reform-minded” budget yet.
Lim, who is also Bagan MP, said expanding the social safety net to gig workers, persons with disabilities and senior citizens, providing more inclusive funding allocations and adjusting personal income tax rates to address past injustices were steps in the right direction.
“These initial steps of budgetary reforms give hope that there will be more future substantial meaningful reforms in the pipeline that will contain cost of living increases, creating sustainable economic growth especially for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and generating prosperity for all by ensuring that there is more money to spend for Malaysian households,” he said in a statement on Facebook.
Still, Lim said more needed to be done, particularly by allocating 10 per cent of total Bumiputera allocations to non-Bumiputera communities without reducing existing Bumiputera funding.
He said this would ensure a fairer and more equitable distribution of taxpayers’ money to non-Bumiputera communities, which he claimed previous governments had neglected.
Earlier, Anwar tabled the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat, outlining the government’s spending plans and direction for the coming year.
Themed “Malaysia Madani:
Menggapai di Langit, Mengakar di Bumi
(Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground),” Budget 2027 is the second Budget under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13), which serves as the national development framework for the 2026-2030 period.

Title: Budget 2027: Medical groups hail end to contract doctor system, enhanced public-private synergy but seek more on retention
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Healthcare stakeholders had mixed responses to the national health allocations announced in Budget 2027, with the Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) applauding the move to end the contract doctor system while highlighting critical gaps in workforce retention
The Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM), meanwhile, welcomed measures to boost public-private cooperation.
The Ministry of Health’s allocation has increased to RM47.7 billion, from RM46.5 billion in 2026.
MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan described the commitment to end the contract doctor system as a major win for the profession, noting that over 9,000 contract doctors are set to be offered permanent positions in 2027.
“This is a significant milestone and addresses one of MMA’s longstanding calls. We commend the Government for taking this important step towards providing greater job security and career certainty for our young doctors,” he said.
He, however, noted that permanent appointments must be accompanied by a broader strategy to retain healthcare workers.
Malaysia faces a shortage of nearly 11,000 specialists, he said, with demand for specialist care expected to rise amid the growing burden of non-communicable diseases (NCDs) and an ageing population.
“We cannot afford to lose more specialists when we urgently need to train and retain more of them,” he said, calling for greater investment in specialist and subspecialist training, career progression, fair remuneration and better working conditions.
MMA also said more emphasis should be placed on strengthening primary healthcare to tackle NCDs.
The country’s network of private general practitioners remains underutilised and could play a greater role in prevention, early detection and long-term disease management, Sivanaesan said.
“Strengthening primary care is essential to reducing avoidable hospital admissions and easing pressure on specialist services,” he said.
Sivanaesan said the success of Budget 2027 should be measured not only by its allocations, but by improvements in patient care, waiting times, workforce retention and access to healthcare.
MMA reiterated its call for a national healthcare workforce distribution dashboard, providing transparent information on staffing levels and shortages at individual public hospitals and clinics. The data could support workforce planning and help direct resources to areas of greatest need, it said.
The association also noted that the RM1.2 billion allocation for hospital and clinic maintenance was unchanged from 2026, despite ageing facilities and growing maintenance needs.
It called for sufficient funding to address manpower shortages in Sabah and Sarawak, including better incentives and career opportunities, and reiterated its call to restore the previous percentage-based Regional Incentive Payment.
Meanwhile, APHM president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh welcomed measures to reduce patient waiting times, including a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing patients to other hospitals and expanded sessional arrangements for private-sector specialists, with the maximum engagement period extended.
APHM also welcomed Budget 2027’s reflection of work on billing transparency, saying it looked forward to further discussions with stakeholders on implementation.
Dr Kuljit said the e-CKAPS portal, which is due to enable private healthcare facilities to be licensed entirely online from 2027, targets a reduction of up to 65 per cent in processing times.
He said faster licensing could also support Malaysia’s medical tourism sector.
“What matters most is not the size of the budget increase but the outcome for patients.
“APHM stands ready to work closely with the Health Ministry and other stakeholders to turn these measures into real improvements on the ground,” he said.

Title: Four injured after lorry crashes into 11 vehicles in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 9 — Four people were injured in an accident involving a lorry and 11 other vehicles at Persiaran Mokhtar Dahari, Alam Budiman here today.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department was informed of the crash at about 4.30pm and immediately dispatched personnel to the scene.
“The accident left a man and a woman with serious head injuries, while two other male victims sustained minor injuries,” he said in a statement.
Ashrul said all the victims were rushed to hospital for further treatment.
Earlier, a video of the incident went viral on social media, showing a lorry believed to have been travelling against the flow of traffic before crashing into several vehicles at the road junction. — Bernama

Title: MEF welcomes RM2,000 minimum wage, says MSME exemption gives smaller firms breathing room
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) today welcomed the federal government’s decision to raise the national minimum wage to RM2,000 while exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with annual sales of less than RM50 million.
The new rate, effective June 2027, was announced earlier by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the tabling of Budget 2027.
MEF senior adviser for government, media and international engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said a balanced approach was essential to ensure efforts to improve workers’ welfare did not inadvertently undermine business viability, discourage hiring or put existing jobs at risk.
“Providing employers until June 2027 is a sensible step that gives businesses the time to plan, adapt and prepare for implementation while minimising disruption to employment and business operations.
“MEF believes that a reasonable transition period, combined with appropriate support for MSMEs, will help ensure that the objective of improving workers’ incomes can be pursued alongside business sustainability and job security,” he said in a statement.
Explaining further, Syed Hussain said a responsible wage policy focuses not only on the extent of wage increases but also on ensuring businesses can sustain those wages, protect existing jobs and continue creating new employment opportunities.
He also noted that while the minimum wage establishes the statutory wage floor, it should not be the ceiling for employers who can afford to pay more.
“MEF encourages employers to reward employees in line with their business performance, productivity, skills and contributions.
“At the same time, we must recognise that businesses have different financial capacities, particularly among MSMEs.
“The ultimate objective is to build sustainable businesses that can continuously create quality jobs and provide better wages for Malaysian workers,” he said.
Regarding the MSME exemption, Syed Hussain said such measures reflect an important recognition that wage policies must account for the differing financial capacities of businesses, particularly smaller enterprises that operate with tighter margins and limited resources.
“While larger businesses may have greater financial capacity to absorb higher labour costs, smaller enterprises often face more significant constraints arising from rising operating expenses, limited access to financing, productivity gaps and the challenges of adopting new technologies.
“An exemption for eligible MSMEs would provide these businesses with greater flexibility to strengthen their financial positions, improve productivity and prepare for future wage adjustments without compromising their ability to sustain employment,” he said.
Nevertheless, Syed Hussain said any exemption should be supported by clear eligibility criteria, transparent implementation guidelines and adequate communication to employers and employees.
This includes clarification on how the annual sales threshold of RM50 million will be assessed, the treatment of related companies and the application of the exemption to different business structures.
He said MEF also proposed that the federal government strengthen complementary measures to help businesses improve productivity and pay higher wages over the longer term.
These include targeted productivity incentives, support for digitalisation and automation, skills development and measures to reduce the cost of doing business, particularly for MSMEs.

Title: Haze: 36 areas record unhealthy API readings, Pasir Gudang highest at 190
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 36 areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.45pm today, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest reading at 190.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Johor that recorded unhealthy API readings were Segamat (187), Larkin (185), Tangkak (183), Batu Pahat (177), Kluang (176), Pengerang (175) and Kota Tinggi (175).
In Negeri Sembilan, three areas recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Seremban (189), Nilai (183) and Port Dickson (174), while in Melaka, the affected areas were Bukit Rambai (187), Bandaraya Melaka (183) and Alor Gajah (181).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest API reading at 181, followed by Shah Alam (175), Petaling Jaya (167), Klang (167), Banting (166) and Kuala Selangor (156).
Cheras and Batu Muda in the capital recorded readings of 177 and 172, respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 170.
Five areas in Perak also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tasek Ipoh (182), Pegoh Ipoh (176), Tanjung Malim (174), Seri Manjung (158) and Taiping (110).
Other affected areas were Rompin (162), Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (158) and Temerloh (156) in Pahang, while in Kedah, Sungai Petani (156) and Alor Setar (152) were affected.
In addition, three areas in Penang also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Minden (154), Seberang Jaya (147) and Seberang Perai (129).
A total of 32 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while no areas recorded good readings.
API readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are considered hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Budget 2027: Government-owned Entities Bill to be drafted next year, RM1.1b for enforcement agencies’ operations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Enforcement agencies, including the police and Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), will receive RM1.1 billion to strengthen their operations under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also the Finance Minister, made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
The government, he said, will also draft a new Government-Owned Entities Act to strengthen good governance in government-owned companies and statutory bodies and prevent major financial scandals such as 1MDB and the mismanagement of Tabung Haji and Felda from recurring.
“With the Government Procurement Act coming to force starting 2027, the government will improve transparency and publish project details, including the contractors and contract value,” Anwar said.
“When governance is corrected, the benefits resulting from the change will contribute to the people’s welfare,” he added.
Anwar also said revenue generated from loan repayments, including from education and business loans, disbursed to federal statutory bodies must only be used for the approved purposes and target groups. This, he said, also applies to interests collected from such loans.
He also singled out the reforms that his administration has achieved since coming to power in 2022, including abolishing mandatory death penalty and penalties for suicide and enacting the Online Safety Act and the Anti-Bullying Act.
“Clearly, the hardest change is the reforms to limit one’s own powers,” he said, referring to the ongoing efforts to secure a two-thirds majority to cap a prime minister’s tenure to two terms.

Title: Budget 2027: Bumiputera contractor procurement nearly doubles to RM7.5b, GLICs to invest RM2b
Article:
