KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government is set to increase the procurement allocation for Bumiputera contractors in the G1 to G4 grades to RM7.5 billion under Budget 2027, an increase from RM4 billion this year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this follows recent concerns raised by Bumiputera contractors and companies.
“For maintenance, repair and upgrading works of government facilities, the procurement threshold for direct appointment is allowed up to RM200,000 and for quotations, up to RM3 million,” he said.
He added that the Unit Peneraju Agenda Bumiputera (Teraju), a strategic agency under the Prime Minister’s Department, will provide financing of up to RM1 billion while effectively monitoring Bumiputera projects across the country.
Meanwhile, financing funds by Perbadanan Usahawan Nasional Berhad (PUNB) will increase from RM350 million previously to RM500 million.
“The government is providing a stamp duty facility of only RM10 for loan and financing agreements under the Cakna II Scheme, which will be introduced from January 1, 2027to December 31, 2030.
“The same facility will also be extended for the Cakna I Scheme until December 31, 2030,” Anwar said.
Government-linked companies (GLCs) and Petronas are targeting RM58 billion procurement from Bumiputera companies while GLC procurement guidelines — which have not been reviewed since 2006 — will be updated next year.
Anwar also announced that government-linked investment companies (GLICs) such as Ekuinas and PHB will also invest RM2 billion to further empower Bumiputera companies while Khazanah Nasional Berhad and Teraju will be introducing the RM250 million
Dana Ciptawan
(Innovators Fund) to support the growth of mid-tier Bumiputera companies.
“Centralised solar parks for government buildings will be developed with an investment of RM1.5 billion.
“This also provides opportunities for Bumiputera construction, engineering, and maintenance companies.
“Through the LSS6 solar project, 150 megawatts is allocated specifically to Bumiputera companies to support them in the clean energy industry,” Anwar said.
He added that the government is also extending the 10 Bumiputera Champions initiative with an allocation of RM40 million to foster 15 potential companies by 2027.

Title: Budget 2027: Government earmarks RM60m for Matrade, RM1b to boost MSME exports
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 - The federal government will allocate RM60 million to the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) to help build local companies’ capacity to enter and diversify their overseas markets, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
In his Budget 2027 speech, Anwar said Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Berhad (BPMB) will also prepare RM1 billion to support local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to explore the export market.
Anwar said the federal government together with the civil servants’ pension fund KWAP will set up a RM50 million UNIVC fund to bring universities’ research to the market, and added that the government will also bear the preliminary risk to enable more private capital to support local inventions.
He said the federal government will also allocate RM142 million for the NADI platform which has enabled many young entrepreneurs to benefit from e-commerce, pointing out that coffee entrepreneur Azmi Warisan from Kampung Sungai Leman, Selangor had successfully increased his revenue by 80 per cent or RM240,000 after using the Nadi platform.
He said JOM Malaysia will also have RM10 million to bring rural products and high-value services to digital platforms and overseas markets.
In support of the low-altitude economy such as those involving drones, Anwar said the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) will invest RM50 million to develop a digital system to manage airspace, national testing site and safety standards.

Title: Budget 2027: Govt rolls out six initiatives to attract global firms, skilled talent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today the federal government will roll out several initiatives in 2027 to make it easier for global companies to operate in Malaysia and attract top skilled talent.
Tabling Budget 2027, Anwar outlined six initiatives to improve Malaysia’s business environment and competitiveness, amid renewed investor confidence in recent years.
“Reformasi Madani has helped restore investor confidence, with Malaysia rising to 15th place in the World Competitiveness Index in two years.
“Malaysia is also ranked as the top destination for digital nomads in the Rumavi Global Relocation Index 2026,” he told the Dewan Rakyat here.
Among other measures, Anwar said the existing Global Services Hub (GSH) incentive will be further improved starting January 2027.
GSH is a Malaysian government tax and business initiative administered by the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida).
“New companies under the GSH incentive will enjoy a special five per cent tax rate on income from GSH activities.
“A five per cent tax rate on income exceeding the baseline income of existing Principal Hub or GSH companies will also be provided.
“The GSH incentive period will also be extended in five-year increments, up to a maximum of 30 years,” he said.
GSH companies managing treasury and fund activities will also be exempted from withholding tax on interest payments and stamp duty on intercompany loan agreements, which also extends to activities under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) package.
Anwar said existing DE Rantau Nomad Pass — Malaysia’s official long-stay digital nomad visa — holders who had reached the two-year limit will be allowed to stay and work remotely in Malaysia for an additional two years, subject to conditions.
Separately, spouses of expatriates holding Category I Employment Passes and Dependant Passes will also be allowed to work in Malaysia, subject to stipulated conditions beginning next year.
“This is aimed at ensuring Malaysia remains an attractive destination for global talent without requiring their spouses to sacrifice their careers,” he said.
Anwar also announced the introduction of the Malaysian Asean Business Entity (MyABE) status to help Malaysian companies develop across Asean.
“The Securities Commission, in collaboration with TalentCorp, will facilitate preliminary Employment Pass applications for listed MyABE companies, with a target processing time of five working days,” he said.
He said the government was also reviewing the Reinvestment Allowance including its eligibility criteria and incentive structure, to make it more targeted and improve industrial competitiveness.
The Reinvestment Allowance is an incentive provided to encourage reinvestment or continued investment by foreign and domestic investors.
Lastly, Anwar said the Securities Commission and Hong Kong regulators would cooperate to facilitate dual listings by Malaysian companies in both markets, providing matching grants to cover listing costs.

Title: Budget 2027: Government halts public university disciplinary proceedings relating to free speech
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has halted disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly with immediate effect.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Higher Education Ministry was preparing a comprehensive legal framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), covering university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights.
“With immediate effect, all disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of speech, expression of views, public criticism and peaceful assembly have been halted,” Anwar told the Parliament today during the tabling of the Budget 2027.
Enacted in 1971, AUKU provides the legal framework for the establishment, administration and governance of public universities. It has long faced criticism over restrictions on student activism and political participation.
The Act was tightened through amendments in 1975 following a wave of student activism, giving university authorities greater powers over student activities and disciplinary action.
Subsequent amendments relaxed some restrictions. Changes in 2012 allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus, while amendments in 2024 transferred disciplinary decisions involving public university students from vice-chancellors to student disciplinary committees.
Despite these changes, student groups continued to call for the Act’s repeal, arguing that it restricted student freedom and participation in public affairs.
Anwar announced in August that the government would repeal AUKU, assuring students that the move would not be followed by new laws that similarly restrict student movements.
The Higher Education Ministry subsequently announced that disciplinary proceedings at public universities relating to freedom of expression, public criticism and peaceful assembly would be stopped immediately while work on the new legal framework continued.
However, the ministry said cases involving violence, vandalism, criminal offences, academic misconduct and breaches of legitimate disciplinary rules would remain subject to existing laws and regulations.

Title: Anwar: Voluntary medical insurance MediAsas to kick off in 2027, EPF Akaun Sejahtera can pay premiums
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — MediAsas, a voluntary medical insurance and takaful plan, will be launched nationwide at affordable prices in January 2027, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
While tabling Budget 2027 at Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said MediAsas would help keep hospital bills under control and more predictable according to diagnosis type.
“Starting 2027, private hospital bills must use a standard and transparent category of charges so that patients understand what they are paying and to reduce price distortions,” he said.
Anwar also said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contributors under 55 years old can also tap into their Akaun Sejahtera to pay for MediAsas premiums.
The government will also extend a subsidy of RM200 per worker for MediAsas premiums for a maximum of 50 employees during the first year for small- and medium-sized enterprises comprising less than 75 employees.
Anwar also said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) will continue implementing the electronic medical records system in all public healthcare facilities nationwide with a RM1 billion allocation.

Title: Budget 2027: Higher Education Ministry gets RM19.1bil, RM800mil for university facilities upgrades
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Higher Education Ministry will receive RM19.1 billion under Budget 2027.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this will include RM800 million to upgrade university facilities and replace ageing equipment.
“The allocation would be used to improve infrastructure such as lecture halls and student accommodation, as well as replace outdated equipment,” Anwar told the Parliament today.
A slight increase from the Budget 2026 allocation of 18.6 billion, the Budget 2027 allocation follows a broader expansion of the ministry’s responsibilities, with Form Six and matriculation students set to come under its purview from 2027, bringing pre-university education within the higher education system.
“The government also welcomes and encourage contributions from the public, alumni and the corporate sector to public universities.
“Donations to public universities would qualify for income tax deductions of up to 10 per cent of aggregate income,” Anwar said.

Title: Budget 2027: Duty‑free shopping limit in Langkawi and Labuan raised to RM10,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The duty-free shopping limit for visitors and tourists in Langkawi and Labuan is set to increase to RM10,000 to boost tourism on the two duty-free islands, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced.
However, Anwar said visitors and tourists must stay for at least 48 hours to enjoy the higher duty-free shopping limit.
“More locally made products from Langkawi will also be exempted from import duties to support local entrepreneurs,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said this when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Addressing difficulties faced by residents and tourists in finding automated teller machines (ATMs) on some resort islands, Anwar said the government will expand QR code payments to 15 locations next year, including resort islands.
He said small traders often miss out on sales when customers did not have cash.
Anwar further announced that government has also extended the Visit Malaysia campaign until next year, with RM935 million allocated for tourism and culture.
He said among the initiatives under the Visit Malaysia campaign are the provision of incentive grants to tourism industry players to promote and organise tourism events.
“The government will also improve the quality of tourism facilities, including jetty infrastructure and heritage sites with the potential to be recognised by Unesco.
“These include Danum Valley in Sabah, Bujang Valley in Kedah and Taman Negara Pahang,” he said.
Anwar also said arts, culture and heritage will continue to receive support through the organisation of a Cultural Festival in conjunction with the SEA Games.
“The government will also support cultural and heritage industry players, including those involved in handicrafts, weaving and batik,” he said.
To improve international connectivity, Anwar said a Matching Grant for International and Charter Flights will be provided to establish new direct flight routes from China, India, Central Asia and Europe.
Anwar said the grant’s scope will be expanded to include cruise ships, ferries and tour buses bringing international tourists to Malaysia.
He also pointed out that Malaysia must become a preferred destination for major international events.
“To attract more such events, rebates will be offered to organisers holding events at venues with a capacity of at least 10,000 spectators.
“Tax incentives for international-standard incentive travel, conferences and trade exhibitions will also be extended until the 2030 year of assessment,” he said.

Title: Budget 2027: e-ART to be main urban public transport solution in Johor Bahru ahead of RTS Link
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today said the Elevated Autonomous Rapid Transit (e-ART) system would be the main solution for easing traffic congestion in Johor Bahru.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would also add bus routes, increase bus and KTM Komuter service frequency, and provide Grab shuttle services in high-demand areas ahead of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link opening next year.
“Traffic congestion in Johor Bahru must be addressed immediately.
“Therefore, the government has agreed to implement the e-ART as the main solution,” he said while tabling Budget 2027 at theDewan Rakyat today.
Anwar said the measure is aimed at improving public transport connectivity and easing traffic congestion as cross-border travel between Johor Bahru and Singapore prepares for a major boost with the RTS Link.
On October 2, the Malaysian and Singaporean governments said Passenger service on the Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link is now expected to begin in February 2027.
In a joint statement, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore (Singapore Grantor) and the Ministry of Transport Malaysia (Malaysia Grantor) said they had been informed by RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) of the revised timeline.

Title: Budget 2027: Entertainment duty exemption for local film, theatre tickets in Federal Territories, creative sector gets RM130m
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Tickets for local films and theatre performances in the Federal Territories will be fully exempt from entertainment duty starting in 2027, as part of the government’s efforts to support the local creative industry.
The government will allocate more than RM130 million to support the film, music and creative content sectors, aimed at enhancing Malaysia’s image, creating jobs and bringing local stories to the international stage, according to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
This includes incentives for local and international film and animation productions that shoot in Malaysia, as well as additional incentives for works that showcase Malaysian culture and national identity.
The government will also strengthen the local animation ecosystem to develop 20 new intellectual properties (IPs) and commercialise Malaysian characters globally.
The government also called on state administrations to introduce similar entertainment duty exemptions to support local creative practitioners.

Title: Budget 2027: Form Six students to receive RM2,500 allowance, early school aid increases to RM200 per pupil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Form Six students will receive a RM2,500 cost-of-living allowance each next year, matching the rate given to matriculation students, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Speaking during the tabling of Budget 2027 in Parliament, Anwar said the assistance would benefit 90,000 Form Six students nationwide.
Anwar also announced that the government would increase Bantuan Awal Persekolahan (BAP), or early schooling assistance, from RM150 to RM200 per pupil next year.
He said the RM1 billion allocation would benefit 5.3 million pupils, with a family of four school-going children receiving RM800 to prepare for the 2027 school session.
“The assistance will be distributed through schools.
“This arrangement would allow parents to meet their children’s teachers in person and reinforce their shared responsibility for pupils’ academic progress and character development,” Anwar said.
The government will also allocate RM870 million for the Supplementary Food Programme (Rancangan Makanan Tambahan), benefiting more than 800,000 pupils.
Anwar said the government would also improve the School Public Donations Fund (Tabung Sumbangan Wang Awam Sekolah) to allow voluntary contributions from parents, alumni and the public to be used for school operations, facility repairs, equipment purchases and student programmes.
Cash contributions to the fund will qualify for tax deductions of up to 10 per cent of aggregate income.
To ease teachers’ administrative workload, the government will expand the recruitment of teaching assistants to 200 primary schools with high pupil enrolment.
“Teachers should return to their task of educating children without being burdened by clerical work,” Anwar said.
Further expansion will take place in phases following an assessment of the programme’s effectiveness.

Title: Budget 2027: 9,000 contract doctors to be made permanent in 2027, incentive hike for paramedics and nurses
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — More than 9,000 contract doctors will be given permanent posting in public healthcare facilities next year, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said the government has offered permanent positions for more than 15,000 contract doctors since 2023, including 4,000 doctors this year alone.
“This means that after this, doctors who complete their housemanship will be offered permanent positions as medical officers,” Anwar said.
Under Budget 2027, the government will also increase post-basic incentives from RM100 to RM200 a month for some 47,000 nurses and paramedics and raise the incentive for Air Health Service staff from RM30 to RM100.

Title: Budget 2027: SMEs to gain up to RM6,000 each from income tax cuts
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — A total of 300,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Malaysia are expected to have additional income of up to RM6,000 each amid expected lower taxes, as the federal government will be cutting their income tax rates, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
As a response to MSMEs’ concerns over rising operating costs, Anwar said the federal government has agreed to reduce their income tax rates by one percentage point:
For the first RM150,000 in taxable income, the tax rate will be reduced to 14 per cent;
For the taxable income from RM150,000 to RM600,000, the tax rate will be reduced to 16 per cent.
Anwar also listed various proposed tax measures, including increasing the limit for each small value assets eligible for capital allowance to RM3,000, while non-MSMEs will have the overall claim limit increased to RM30,000.
Another proposed measure is to allow manufacturers to claim sales tax on machines, replacement parts and equipment purchased from farmers or local distributors, which will cover raw materials to produce pharmaceutical products, animal feed, fertiliser and pesticides.
Anwar said the government also proposes to extend the existing Accelerated Capital Allowance on capital expenditure for plant, machinery and ICT equipment for businesses until December 31, 2030.
He said the government will also propose only RM10 in stamp duty for loans through peer-to-peer platforms from January 1, 2027 until December 31, 2030, and full stamp duty exemption for the opening of saving accounts and current accounts starting from January 1, 2027.
To ease MSMEs’ cash flow via credit facilities from banks for mid-tier companies, he also said the government proposes a stamp duty of only RM10 for agreements to use credit excess that are completed from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2030.

Title: Anwar: MA63 a national promise, 12 items finalised, more scholarships for Sabah and Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) should be seen as part of a “
Waad Nasional
” or national promise and a national responsibility that must receive a national response, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today in his Budget 2027 speech.
Referring to the agreement which was signed between the founding partners of Malaysia, Anwar said that 12 items under MA63 have been finalised so far, and also listed other measures and allocations that the federal government has been channelling to Sabah and Sarawak.
Anwar said the federal government has agreed to increase Public Service Department (JPA) scholarship offers to Sabah and Sarawak’s students.
“This means 4,200 Sabahans and Sarawakians will get the opportunity to further their studies every year,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat.
In his speech, Anwar noted that the federal government’s special grants over the past decades for Sabah and Sarawak had not been in line with their developmental needs.
He said the current federal government has increased these special grants three times, with the latest interim payment being RM1.5 billion, and that there would be continued talks with Sabah and Sarawak to finalise a fair and sustainable annual formula.
Among the 12 items in MA63 which had been finalised under the current government are permanent representatives from Sabah and Sarawak in the Inland Revenue Board and the Bintulu port becoming a Sarawak-owned port.
They also include Sarawak taking over MASWings, which is now known as AirBorneo, while the federal government still provides RM209 million in subsidies to benefit 820,000 passengers in the interiors; and handing over electricity regulatory powers to Sabah while the federal government continues providing RM600 million to ensure continued electricity supply.
Anwar said the proposed federal allocation for Sabah and Sarawak next year remains the highest, with Sabah to receive RM18.7 billion in 2027 (as compared to RM17.6 billion this year) and Sarawak to receive RM16.2 billion (as compared to RM15.1 billion).
Among other things, Anwar said RM3.3 billion has been allocated next year to continue road and highway projects in Sabah and Sarawak.
Noting that the Sarawak state government has expressed intent to develop a special economic zone in Sibu, Anwar said the federal government has started official talks to finalise the framework for incentives, one-stop centre to facilitate investments and strategic infrastructure needs.

Title: Budget 2027: Health Ministry allocation increased, RM1.2b earmarked for upgrading of public facilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The Health Ministry will receive RM47.7 billion next year, up from this year’s RM46.5 billion, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
While tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today, Anwar said RM1.2 billion will be distributed for repair, upgrade and maintenance works of all public hospitals and clinics.
A total of nine new facilities, including a specialist clinic complex and daycare treatment centre at Hospital Sultanah Aminah in Johor, will also be constructed next year, Anwar said.
“More than RM770 million will also be allocated for the procurement of modern and sophisticated equipment to speed up diagnosis and treatment,” Anwar said.
The new assets, he said, would include haemodialysis facilities in hospitals nationwide, 400 new government ambulances, a specialist hospital under Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) with robotic surgery expertise as well as clinical simulation equipment and science laboratories in 18 training institutes.
Anwar also announced a RM200 million allocation for outsourcing of patients to other hospitals to reduce waiting period.

Title: Budget 2027: School repair allocation doubles to RM2b, dilapidated schools get RM1.3b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — School repair allocation is set to be doubled to RM2 billion next year.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the Budget 2027 in Parliament, said the allocation increase would cover different types of schools, including national schools, Chinese and Tamil national-type schools, as well as registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools.
“The allocation for national schools will increase to RM900 million, while Chinese national-type schools will receive RM100 million and Tamil national-type schools, RM50 million.
“Registered religious schools, tahfiz institutions and pondok schools under the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim) will receive RM200 million, with the scope of funding expanded to cover their operating costs.
“The government recognises the urgent need to improve infrastructure at Tamil national-type schools despite their relatively smaller enrolment,” Anwar told Parliament today.
Separately, nearly RM1.3 billion will be allocated to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
These allocations are part of the Education Ministry’s huge allocation of RM69 billion under the Budget 2027, up from RM66.2 billion this year.
“To accommodate an expected 500,000 pupils entering Year One next year, including more than 70,000 aged six, the government expects to complete 3,500 additional classrooms by the end of this year using the Industrialised Building System (IBS),” Anwar added.
The Prime Minister also announced plans for new schools, preschool buildings and additional facilities at existing schools, including SK Seri Chemor in Ipoh, Perak; Kompleks Sekolah Bandar Serenia in Sepang, Selangor; and a replacement building for SJK (Tamil) Ladang Pamol in Kluang, Johor.
Other projects include SJK (C) Bandar Mahkota Cheras and a preschool building at SK Bulu Silou in Keningau, Sabah.
A new matriculation college is also being built in Marang, Terengganu.

Title: Budget 2027: Road Transport Act to be amended to require drunk, drug-impaired drivers to compensate victims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Existing road transport law will be amended to make it mandatory for motorists driving under the influence to pay compensation to victims.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the amendments would cover driving under the influence of both alcohol and drugs under the Road Transport Act.
Four people, including three family members, were killed and three others injured in a collision involving 11 vehicles at KM110.4 of the LPT1, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit in Lanchang, Temerloh, at about 10 pm on August 31.
Citing the crash, Anwar said such tragedies were deeply distressing and showed that road safety violations remained a concern despite tighter enforcement.
“As of August, 28 fatal cases involving drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs had been recorded.
“Therefore, as a sterner measure, the government will amend the Road Transport Act,” he said while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar also said a telematics system will be made compulsory for installation on commercial vehicles to monitor speed, location and risky driving patterns, including links to alcohol detection devices to check drivers before they begin their journeys.
“Voluntary implementation will continue until 2027 while the government develops a database of drivers for enforcement purposes,” he said.
He also said the Social Security Organisation (Socso) will provide health screening vouchers for commercial vehicle drivers to detect medical risks that could affect their ability to drive safely.

Title: Chinese New Villages, non‑Muslim houses of worship to receive bigger allocations under Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The federal government today announced an increase in allocations for the maintenance of Chinese New Villages and non-Muslim houses of worship from 2027 onwards.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the allocation for infrastructure upgrades in Chinese New Villages will be increased to more than RM100 million, including repairs and rebuilding of ageing facilities.
“Meanwhile, funding for the maintenance of registered non-Muslim houses of worship will also be increased to RM80 million,” he said during the tabling of Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat here today.
Separately, Anwar said the ongoing Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives have benefitted nearly 500 villages and 1,700 schools nationwide since 2024.
Therefore, the government will introduce the Komuniti Angkat Madani initiative with an allocation of RM50 million for 2027, focusing on helping urban People’s Housing Project (PPR) communities.
“For example, the Attorney General’s Chambers provided facilities in Kampung Jilid 8 in Kuala Muda, Kedah, including a football field, a fishermen’s jetty and a Bank Simpanan Nasional ATM, which also benefit residents of neighbouring villages.
“Meanwhile, SK Telok Kalong in Terengganu received a comfortable special remedial classroom and robotics learning facilities for pupils through contributions from Sime Darby Berhad,” he said.
He then expressed his appreciation to the management of ministries, departments and agencies, as well as corporate bodies, for contributing to the initiatives.

Title: Budget 2027: Relief for caregivers as service tax for older citizens’ care reduced, new tax exemptions and increased financial aid announced
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The service tax rate for elderly care services will be reduced from eight to six per cent, starting January 1, 2027.
A full exemption will also be granted on care fees up to RM96,000 a year.
Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement while tabling Budget 2027 at the Dewan Rakyat today.
Anwar said the government will also increase financial aid for senior citizens to RM1.3 billion next year, benefiting nearly 200,000 recipients.
“The government will also draft a Senior Citizens Bill to tackle neglect (of the elderly) and strengthen the care ecosystem as a whole,” he said.
“More than 40 million ringgit will also be allocated to HRD Corp to train 8,000 people in the elderly care sector and open job opportunities for them,” he added.
Two National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) will also be developed in Penang and Sarawak to support training, research and elderly care, Anwar said.
On a related development, Anwar said Employees Provident Fund (EPF) members aged 55 and 60 can opt for monthly withdrawals under i-Emas so that their remaining savings can continue generating dividends.

Title: Budget 2027: Govt allocates RM80b for subsidies, STR and SARA rises to RM16b
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government expects to spend more than RM80 billion on subsidies, assistance and incentives next year.
Tabling Budget 2027 in Parliament, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said fuel subsidies were expected to remain high at RM40 billion, while assistance through the Social Welfare Department would amount to nearly RM3.3 billion.
“The government will also increase the allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM16 billion next year, up from RM15 billion this year.
“All STR recipients would receive SARA assistance of up to RM150 a month, or RM1,800 annually, benefiting up to nine million recipients.
“Non-STR recipients aged 18 and above will also receive RM100 in SARA Madani credit twice next year, once before Hari Raya Aidilfitri and another ahead of the 70th anniversary of Merdeka.
“The two payments are expected to benefit up to 13 million Malaysians, including those in the middle 40 (M40) income group,” Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, told Parliament today.
The government will also expand the use of SARA credits to include fresh produce sold at 216
pasar tani
(farmers’ market) and
tamu
(open-air markets) under Fama nationwide.
There are currently 15,000 SARA partner outlets, including 6,800 small grocery shops and cooperatives.
The government aims to increase the number of participating small grocery shops to 10,000 before the end of this year.
Separately, the allocation for Jualan Rahmah Madani and Jualan Agro Madani will rise to RM750 million from RM630 million, with 35,000 sales events targeted next year.
Of these, 30,000 Jualan Rahmah events will be held across all state constituencies, with greater emphasis on rural areas, low-cost housing areas and urban People’s Housing Project (PPR) communities.
The programme will also expand beyond conventional grocery shops to include vending machines, while Jualan Rahmah Madani Borong will help small traders.
Another 5,000 Jualan Agro Madani events will offer fresh agricultural produce, including fish, chicken, vegetables and fruits, at prices up to 30 per cent lower.
The government will also allocate RM250 million to expand the distribution of essential goods to rural and remote areas, including six new locations such as Kampung Terian in Penampang, Sabah, and Kampung Dato’ Godam in Pusa, Sarawak.

Title: Government allocates RM3.3b for rural infrastructure, RM2.5b to replace ageing water pipes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The allocation for rural road projects will be increased to RM2.3 billion, compared to RM1.3 billion in 2022.
In his Budget speech today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that a total of RM3.3 billion will be allocated for rural basic infrastructure projects, including the installation of village streetlights, community facilities, and clean water and electricity supply.
Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) is installing solar-powered streetlights in villages and rooftop solar panels at welfare homes and places of worship.
Electricity supply will also be improved at tahfiz schools, pondok religious schools and Orang Asli settlements.
Additionally, the Madani administration has successfully facilitated an agreement between the Perak and Penang state governments through a 40-year Bulk Water Supply Agreement.
Access to clean water nationwide will continue to be improved through the National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) programme, with an allocation of RM2.5 billion.
The focus will be on replacing 1,900 kilometres of ageing, critical water pipes.

Title: Budget 2027: Stamp duty exemption proposed for first homes up to RM500,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — The government has proposed a full stamp duty exemption on loan agreements and instruments of transfer for first homes priced up to RM500,000, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
Anwar also said the government would provide a full exemption on the first RM500,000 and a 50 per cent exemption on the remaining amount for first homes priced up to RM750,000.
“The exemptions would apply to sale and purchase agreements executed from January 1, 2027, to December 31, 2030,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said this when tabling the Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.
In a separate measure aimed at eliminating abandoned housing projects by 2030, Anwar said the government will also provide full stamp duty exemptions on loan agreements and instruments of transfer executed between rehabilitating contractors or developers and the original purchasers.
“The exemption for abandoned housing projects will also take effect from January 1, 2027, to December 31, 2030,” he said.

Title: Budget 2027: All Malaysians to be automatically registered with EPF at 18
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — All Malaysian citizens will be automatically registered as members of the Employees Provident Fund (EPF) upon turning 18 to encourage earlier retirement savings, under a measure announced in Budget 2027.
The move aims to strengthen social protection by helping Malaysians prepare for retirement from a younger age.
Currently, employees are automatically registered with the EPF when the fund receives their first employer contribution.
Individuals can also register through the EPF’s i-Akaun application.
The EPF is Malaysia’s main retirement savings fund, with contributions from employees and employers helping members build savings for their later years.

Title: Budget 2027: DBKL to get RM400m for 120 acres of parks, walkways and upgraded facilities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 9 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) will be allocated RM400 million to create 120 acres of new green spaces and upgrade public facilities as part of efforts to make the capital more liveable.
During the tabling of Budget 2027 today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the plans include a 22km of covered pedestrian walkways linking landmarks such as the National Mosque, Dataran Merdeka and Central Market, as well as connecting public housing to schools, clinics and transport hubs.
A 100-acre leasehold site in Bukit Kiara is also being gazetted as a federal park, while buggy services are to be introduced for visitors, particularly elderly travellers, heading to destinations such as the National Monument, Botanical Gardens and Carcosa Seri Negara.
Anwar also commended Khazanah Nasional’s Warisan KL initiative, which has drawn 500,000 visitors following the restoration of the Sultan Abdul Samad Building. The next phase of conservation will focus on Dayabumi Tower, Kuala Lumpur Railway Station and the KTMB headquarters.
Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) was recognised for restoring Merdeka Stadium, with the National Stadium next in line.
Anwar said entertainment duty will be exempted for arts, cultural and sporting events at both venues to encourage greater use.
He added that two DBKL buildings, the Anjung Kelana Homeless Transformation Centre in Taman Desa and the Cheras Temporary Market, will be upgraded into day centres for senior citizens.
